interest: Japanese bid for a U.S. Army equestrian visit, 1935.
overview: This file contains diplomatic correspondence from January and February 1935 concerning an initiative by Shingoro Takaishi, Editor-in-Chief of the Osaka Mainichi and Tokyo Nichi-Nichi, to invite United States Army equestrians to Japan for joint exhibitions in Tokyo and Osaka. Backed by Imperial Prince Higashikuni and Lieutenant General Oshima of the Nippon Equestrian Society, the proposal offered full funding for American military riders and was endorsed by U.S. Ambassador Joseph C. Grew and Military Attaché Major Crane as a constructive goodwill endeavor reminiscent of Baron Takeichi Nishi's acclaim at the 1932 Los Angeles Olympics. However, upon referral from the Department of State, the War Department Chief of Staff declined the invitation on the grounds that training and preparations for the upcoming 1936 Olympic Games precluded sending army riders and horses to Japan.

subfiles.about: Ambassador Joseph C. Grew reports on a proposal by Japanese newspaper editor Shingoro Takaishi to invite American Army equestrians to Japan for exhibitions in Tokyo and Osaka.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, U.S. Ambassador to Japan
subfiles.summary: Grew forwards Takaishi's invitation for U.S. Army riders to exhibitions in Japan, which he supports.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1124 from Ambassador Joseph C. Grew on Proposed Equestrian Exhibition

subfiles.about: Shingoro Takaishi formally requests Ambassador Grew's assistance in securing permission for U.S. Army equestrians to participate in exhibitions in Japan.
subfiles.from: Shingoro Takaishi, Editor in Chief, The Tokyo Nichi-Nichi
subfiles.summary: Takaishi asks Grew to seek War Department approval for an equestrian visit.
subfiles.title: Letter from Shingoro Takaishi to Ambassador Grew Proposing Equestrian Visit (Enclosure No. 1)
subfiles.to: Joseph C. Grew, U.S. Ambassador to Japan

subfiles.about: Shingoro Takaishi informs Ambassador Grew of reports that the War Department disfavors the equestrian visit and appeals for official reconsideration.
subfiles.from: Shingoro Takaishi, Editor in Chief, The Tokyo Nichi-Nichi
subfiles.summary: Takaishi asks Grew to press the proposal despite War Department doubts.
subfiles.title: Letter from Shingoro Takaishi to Ambassador Grew Requesting Further Consideration (Enclosure No. 2)
subfiles.to: Joseph C. Grew, U.S. Ambassador to Japan

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State transmits Ambassador Grew's despatch and enclosures to the Secretary of War for an expression of views.
subfiles.summary: State refers the equestrian invitation to the Secretary of War.
subfiles.title: Department of State Referral to Secretary of War regarding Equestrian Exhibition

subfiles.about: The War Department declines the invitation for American Army officers to participate in the exhibition due to 1936 Olympic preparations.
subfiles.from: General, Chief of Staff, War Department
subfiles.summary: The Army declines, citing preparation for the 1936 Olympics.
subfiles.title: Letter from War Department Chief of Staff Declining Equestrian Invitation

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State informs Ambassador Grew that the War Department has declined the equestrian invitation due to preparations for the 1936 Olympic Games.
subfiles.summary: State tells Grew the Army declined the equestrian invitation.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 698 from Secretary of State to Ambassador Grew on War Department Decision
subfiles.to: Joseph C. Grew, U.S. Ambassador to Japan
